_meta.indication: AGAMREE is indicated for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients 2 years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel group, placebo- and active-controlled; Period 1 randomized to placebo, vamorolone 2.0 mg/kg, vamorolone 6.0 mg/kg, or prednisone 0.75 mg/kg/day for 24 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Ambulant boys with DMD between 4 to <7 years of age who were corticosteroid naive
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in TTSTAND velocity for vamorolone 6.0 mg/kg compared with placebo at Week 24
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean change in TTSTAND velocity 0.0483 rises/sec (vamorolone 6.0 mg/kg) vs -0.012 rises/sec (placebo), a difference of 0.0603 rises/sec (95% CI 0.023, 0.0976), p=0.0018. Key secondary 6MWT distance greater improvement by 41.586 meters (95% CI 14.232, 68.940), p=0.0033.

nct_ctgov.title: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Vamorolone in Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10% and greater than placebo): cushingoid features (29% at 6 mg/kg vs 0% placebo), psychiatric disorders (21% vs 14%), vomiting (14% vs 7%), weight increased (11% vs 3%), and vitamin D deficiency (11% vs 0%).
target_moa: Vamorolone acts as an agonist of the glucocorticoid receptor to reduce NF-kB mediated gene transcription; it is also an antagonist of the mineralocorticoid receptor. The precise mechanism in DMD is unknown.
modality: Small molecule (steroidal anti-inflammatory drug / corticosteroid); a 9,11-glucocorticoid analogue

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable, the trial design is acceptable, and the efficacy findings were clear.

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy Designation was denied (May 21, 2018 and again December 6, 2021) because vamorolone did not demonstrate substantial clinical improvement or safety over existing therapies.

citations.quote: Breakthrough Therapy Designation was denied on May 21, 2018, because the sponsor did not provide any clinical data demonstrating substantial improvement on one or more clinically significant endpoints over the existing therapies approved for DMD.

On December 6, 2021, the Agency issued a Deny Breakthrough Therapy Designation determination because based on the data provided in the request, vamorolone did not demonstrate substantial clinical improvement or safety over existing therapies.

summary.text: AGAMREE received a standard (not priority) review as a new molecular entity; the application was received October 26, 2022. Vamorolone had orphan drug designation (granted December 2, 2011) and Fast Track designation (granted March 15, 2017); Breakthrough Therapy Designation was denied. Approval was based on a single adequate and well-controlled study (VBP15-004); this was a traditional approval, not an accelerated approval.

requirement.text: 4515-3 Conduct a trial to evaluate the CYP3A4 induction potential of vamorolone in a dedicated clinical drug-drug interaction study to address the serious risk of altered pharmacokinetics of CYP3A4 substrates when used with vamorolone. The study will be an open-label, fixed-sequence phase 1 study conducted in healthy volunteers (male and female). A specific CYP3A4 substrate (e.g., midazolam) would be administered on Day 1. After a sufficient washout, vamorolone would be administered at the highest dose (6 mg/kg) for sufficient duration to induce CYP3A4 (usually around 10-14 days), followed by the administration of specific CYP3A4 substrate along with vamorolone. Pharmacokinetics of the CYP3A4 substrate would be evaluated before and after vamorolone administration to assess the magnitude of CYP3A4 induction.
